title: DSX project configuration v1
description: Strict, reviewable project configuration for one DSX Linux ARM64 workspace. CLI flags override project values; defaults have lower precedence.

$schema.description: Editor schema URI for DSX configuration v1.

schemaVersion.description: Configuration format version. Version 1 is the only accepted value.

workspace.description: Workspace root and optional composite repository members.

image.description: Pinned Linux ARM64 image reference, reviewed project build, or DSX-owned standard image.

setup.description: Approved setup commands, executed in order when relevant inputs invalidate setup state.

processes.description: Named processes and services supervised inside the integrated workspace.

volumes.description: Named DSX-owned writable volumes; host paths are not volumes.

mounts.description: Explicit workspace, DSX volume, or reviewed host-directory mounts.

authProfiles.description: Named harness authentication profiles and their persistence scope.

browser.description: Opt-in isolated browser request; release support remains evidence-gated.

aws.description: Opt-in standard AWS/Leapp directory grant; never contains credential values.

network.description: Internet access and destination-specific host TCP grants.

ports.description: Host publications for guest TCP ports; omitted bind defaults to loopback and non-loopback values are explicit trust grants.

resources.description: Workspace CPU, memory, and clone-concurrency limits.

name.description: Lowercase user-visible identifier used for processes, profiles, members, ports, grants, or volumes.

projectPath.description: Non-empty path interpreted relative to the canonical project root unless a field says otherwise.

guestPath.description: Absolute path inside the Linux workspace.

workspace.description: Canonical project-relative workspace root and optional repository member layout.

root.description: Workspace root relative to the project root; normally a single dot.

members.description: Repositories reproduced at the declared relative paths in composite clone mode.

member.description: One named repository in a composite workspace.

name.description: Exact member selector accepted by dsx git --repo.

path.description: Member repository path relative to the workspace root.

image.description: Exactly one prebuilt image reference, reviewed local build definition, or DSX-owned standard image.

ref.description: Linux ARM64 OCI image reference; release configurations should pin a digest.

build.description: Reviewed local OCI image build inputs.

standard.description: Build or reuse the DSX-owned standard Ubuntu agent image.

imageBuild.description: Project-relative build context, file, optional target, and nonsecret build arguments.

context.description: Build context relative to the project root.

file.description: Build file relative to the project root.

args.description: Nonsecret build arguments; secrets must not be placed in image build arguments.

command.description: One executable command expressed either as an argv array or an explicit shell plus shellPath.

argv.description: Structured executable and argument array; no host shell interpolation is performed.

shell.description: Explicit guest shell script. This is executable authority and changes the approval hash.

shellPath.description: Exact supported guest shell interpreter required when shell is used.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory inside the guest.

env.description: Environment values, host-variable references, or secret references passed to this command.

envValue.description: Exactly one literal, named host environment lookup, or secret reference.

value.description: Literal nonsecret value recorded in the effective plan.

hostEnv.description: Exact host environment variable name resolved at execution; do not put the secret value in config.

secretRef.description: Opaque secret-store reference; DSX plans and diagnostics retain only this reference.

process.description: Supervised guest process using the same command forms plus dependency, readiness, and terminal metadata.

shell.description: Explicit guest shell script; shellPath is required and argv is forbidden.

dependsOn.description: Process names that must become ready before this process starts.

required.description: Whether failure makes the sandbox failed.

terminal.description: Whether the process requests terminal semantics instead of separate stdout/stderr streams.

health.description: Optional readiness check used by dependencies and agent/browser launch.
Exactly one HTTP, TCP, or command health probe with optional timing policy.

url.description: Absolute URL probed from inside the workspace.

address.description: Host and port probed from inside the workspace.

command.description: Guest command whose successful exit indicates readiness.

interval.description: Go-style duration between attempts, for example 1s.

retries.description: Number of retry attempts after an unsuccessful probe.

volume.description: One DSX-owned writable volume mounted at a guest path.

scope.description: Whether clone sandboxes receive independent state or share project-scoped state.

persistent.description: Whether stop/recreation preserves the volume; clean still removes owned project resources.

mountSource.description: Exactly one workspace path, named DSX volume, or canonical absolute host path.

type.description: Authority class of the mount source.

path.description: Project-relative path for workspace sources or canonical absolute path for host sources.

volume.description: Exact key from the top-level volumes object.

mount.description: Explicit source-to-guest-target mount. Host-directory mounts must be read-only.

target.description: Absolute target path inside the workspace.

readOnly.description: Read-only mount request; required by semantic validation for host sources.

agents.description: Harness selection policy for this project.

default.description: Harness selected when no CLI override is provided.

allowed.description: Harnesses permitted for this project; the default must be included.

authProfile.description: Harness-bound credential profile with project/sandbox or global persistence.

harness.description: Only this harness may use the profile.

persistence.description: sandbox scopes state to a sandbox; global survives ordinary project cleanup.

enabled.description: Request a separate zero-mount browser VM on the owning private network; the CLI flag may enable but not disable this approved value.

aws.description: Standard AWS behavior using no grant or an opt-in read-only Leapp directory.

mode.description: none disables AWS host credentials; leapp requires a reviewed directory and permits an optional profile.

directory.description: Canonical physical, non-symlink host directory mounted read-only in Leapp mode; it must contain regular config and credentials files, and every profile in them may be readable.

profile.description: Standard AWS_PROFILE selection convenience; this is not credential isolation.

network.description: Workspace internet policy and explicit single-destination host TCP grants.

internet.description: Permit public internet access; enabling the isolated browser requires it.

hostGrants.description: Hash-covered TCP destinations reachable through temporary project-scoped relays when required.

hostGrant.description: One immutable hostname-or-IP and TCP port; URLs, paths, generic proxies, and UDP are not accepted.

destination.description: Exact hostname or IP address without scheme, path, credentials, or port.

port.description: One guest TCP port published to the macOS loopback interface.

name.description: Unique display name for the URL/mapping.

guest.description: TCP port listened on inside the workspace.

host.description: Request runtime-selected allocation with dynamic or one fixed host port.

bind.description: Host IP to bind. Omitting it defaults to 127.0.0.1; any non-loopback value is an explicit trust grant.

resources.description: Per-workspace resource and project clone-concurrency limits.

memory.description: Positive binary memory quantity in MiB or GiB.

maxConcurrentClones.description: Maximum running named clone sandboxes for this project; DSX fails rather than queues beyond it.
